profile.name: VARUN KUMAR
profile.title: Embedded Systems Engineer | C/C++ Firmware | RTOS | Driver Development
profile.degree: B.Tech in Electronics and Computer Engineering
profile.university: Vels University, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India
profile.bio: Embedded engineer writing C/C++ firmware and device drivers for ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers (STM32, ESP32). Experienced in FreeRTOS task design, interrupt handling (NVIC, EXTI), register-level drivers, and hardware-firmware debugging with JTAG/SWD, OpenOCD, GDB, and logic analyzers. Has built containerized CI/CD pipelines for firmware validation.
profile.availability: Available for full-time embedded engineering roles and technical discussions.

projects.title: STM32F030x4 Peripheral Driver Library
projects.subtitle: Register-Level Embedded C Drivers (No Vendor HAL)
projects.description: Wrote bare-metal device drivers for GPIO, RCC, NVIC, EXTI, SYSCFG, ADC, SPI, and I2C on the STM32F030x4 (ARM Cortex-M0, 16 KB flash, 4 KB SRAM) using register-level Embedded C, without relying on vendor HAL.
projects.problem: Vendor HAL abstractions often introduce execution overhead, opaque interrupt handlers, and multi-layer abstraction bloat that make timing-critical peripheral control difficult to trace and optimize on constrained 16 KB Flash microcontrollers.
projects.approach: Direct register-level bitfield manipulation referencing the RM0360 Reference Manual and Cortex-M0 Generic User Guide. Built complete custom startup assembly, linker script, and Makefile toolchain with arm-none-eabi-gcc.
projects.implementation: Authored modular drivers for 8 core peripherals (GPIO with atomic BSRR bit set/reset, RCC system clock and prescalers, NVIC interrupt priorities, EXTI line routing, ADC 12-bit conversions, SPI master framing, I2C timing bitfields).
projects.debugging: Isolated bus synchronization and peripheral clock gating issues using OpenOCD over ST-Link SWD with GDB hardware breakpoints and an 8-channel logic analyzer to verify SPI and I2C protocol framing.
projects.validation: Verified clock tree configuration, GPIO switching speeds, SPI transmission framing, and I2C Start/Stop timing on physical target hardware with 17+ structured commits and public documentation.

projects.title: Smart Number Plate for Theft Detection
projects.subtitle: Real-Time Embedded Vehicle Security Prototype
projects.description: Developed bare-metal and FreeRTOS-based firmware on an ARM microcontroller for vehicle theft detection and actuator lockout control with real-time responsiveness.
projects.problem: Vehicle security systems require deterministic response times between wireless RFID tag interrogation, sensor telemetry acquisition, and physical actuator control without task starvation or deadlock.
projects.approach: Preemptive FreeRTOS multitasking architecture using thread-safe message queues and binary semaphores for inter-task communication and non-blocking ISR signal handling.
projects.implementation: Implemented RFID protocol handling, closed-loop feedback control logic for ignition lockout, and hardware protection circuits.
projects.debugging: Validated signal timing with a logic analyzer and debugged hardware-firmware integration issues using OpenOCD and GDB.
projects.validation: Measured actuator response timing from unauthorized motion trigger to lockout signal and verified queue stability during rapid RFID scanning tests.

projects.title: Embedded UI Designer (Final Year Project)
projects.subtitle: Desktop UI Design Tool & Firmware Code Generation
projects.description: Built a desktop UI design tool for embedded systems with an SDK, a type-safe REST API engine, and multi-language firmware code generation for microcontrollers.
projects.problem: Designing embedded graphical interfaces and mapping visual widgets to microcontroller memory buffers often requires repetitive manual C coordinate math and boilerplate driver code.
projects.approach: Visual interface canvas coupled with an automated code generator translating interactive design elements into compact, type-safe C/C++ firmware data structures and rendering callbacks.
projects.implementation: Created cross-platform desktop UI software supporting element styling, type-safe API communication, and automated C/C++ header and source code emission tailored for constrained displays.
projects.debugging: Profiled generated code memory overhead and verified buffer compatibility across display drivers.
projects.validation: Successfully generated firmware UI assets validated for microcontroller display integration.

projects.title: Open Source Systems Contributions
projects.subtitle: LLVM Backend Optimizations & ARM System Porting
projects.description: Contributed to low-level open source systems: compiler backend improvements in Gravel Launcher (LLVM performance) and SolidCraft system function porting to ARM architectures (Windows on ARM & Linux ARM).
projects.problem: Compilers and cross-platform native software require deep architecture-specific instruction knowledge to optimize code emission and support ARM hardware platforms reliably.
projects.approach: System-level profiling, LLVM IR visitor pass optimization, and POSIX / Windows ARM API abstraction porting.
projects.implementation: Refined tokenizer and AST construction in Gravel Launcher; implemented ARM system call and runtime function mappings in SolidCraft.
projects.debugging: Used GDB, Valgrind, and regression test suites to track memory lifetimes and ARM cross-compilation target compatibility.
projects.validation: Verified builds on both x86_64 and ARM64 target environments with upstream merged commits.
